XXVI.}}</noinclude>and yet more mad against them, I persecuted them euen vnto foraine cities. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=12}}† Among vvhich things vvhiles {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 9, 3.''}}* I vvent to Damascus vvith authoritie and permission of the cheefe priests, {{verse|chapter=26|verse=13}}† at midday, in the vvay, I savv (o king) from heauen a light to haue shined round about me and them that vvere in companie vvith me, aboue the brightnes of the sunne. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=14}}† And vvhen al vve vvere fallen dovvne on the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew tongue: Saul, Saul, vvhy persecutest thou me? It is hard for thee to kicke against the pricke. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=15}}† And I said, Vvho art thou Lord? And our Lord ansvvered, I am {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhom thou doest persecute. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=16}}† But rise vp and stand vpon thy feete: for to this end haue I appeared to thee, that I may ordaine thee a minister and vvitnes of those things vvhich thou hast seen, and of those things vvherein I vvil appeare to thee, {{verse|chapter=26|verse=17}}† deliuering thee out of the peoples & nations vnto the vvhich novv I send thee, {{verse|chapter=26|verse=18}}† to open their eies, that they may be conuerted from darkenes to light, and from the povver of Satan to God, that they may receiue remission of sinnes and lot among the saincts by the faith that is in me. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=19}}† Vvherevpon, king Agrippa, I vvas not incredulous to the heauenly vision: {{verse|chapter=26|verse=20}}† but to them first that are at Damascus, and at Hierusalem, and vnto al the countrie of Ievvrie, and to the Gentiles {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 9, 20.''}}* did I preach that they should doe {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Penance often inculcated, and vvorkes agreable to the same. · Act. 9, 20.}}∷ penance, and turne to God, doing vvorkes vvorthie of penance. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=21}}† For this cause the Iewes, vvhen I vvas in the temple, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 21, 30.''}}* apprehending me, attempted meaning to kil me. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=22}}† But aided by the help of God, I stand vntil this day, testifying to small and to great, saying nothing beside those things vvhich the Prophets did speake should come to passe, & Moyses, {{verse|chapter=26|verse=23}}† if {{sc|C h r}} I S T vvere passible, if the first of the resurrection from the dead, he vvere to shevv light to the people and to the Gentiles.

{{verse|chapter=26|verse=24}}† As he spake these things and made his ansvver, Festus vvith a loud voice said, Thou art mad, Paul: much learning turneth thee to madnesse. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=25}}† And Paul said, I am not mad, most excellent Festus: but I speake vvordes of veritie and sobrietie. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=26}}† for the king knovveth of these things, to vvhom also I speake constantly. for I thinke none of these things to be vnknovven to him. For neither vvas any of these things done in a corner. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=27}}† Beleeuest thou the prophets, king Agrippa? I knovv that thou beleeuest. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=28}}† And Agrippa said to Paul: A<noinclude>{{rh|||litle}}</noinclude>
